app.title: Which Linux?
app.tagline: Answer a few questions. Get a distribution that actually fits you.
progress.label: Question {current} of {total}
nav.pickOne: Pick at least one to continue
nav.hintKeys: Tip: press 1-9 to choose, Backspace to go back.
question.device.title: What are you setting up? 💻
question.device.hint: Everything else follows from this, so let's start here.
question.arch.title: What's inside it?
question.arch.hint: If you have no idea, it is almost certainly a regular PC.
option.arch.arm: An ARM device (Raspberry Pi and friends)
question.ram.title: How much memory does it have?
question.ram.hint: Memory, not storage. Anything bought in the last few years has 8 GB or more.
option.ram.under4: Under 4 GB — it's an older machine
option.ram.8plus: 8 GB or more — it can run Crysis
question.terminal.title: How do you feel about the terminal?
question.terminal.hint: The black window full of text. There is no wrong answer here.
option.terminal.never: I would rather never see it
option.terminal.paste: Happy to paste in a command now and then
option.terminal.tinker: I enjoy tinkering under the hood 🔧
question.stability.title: Stability, or the newest software?
question.stability.hint: Linux lets you choose. Most people are happiest somewhere in the middle.
option.stability.stable: If it works, don't break it 🛡️
question.familiarity.title: Which of these feels most like home?
question.familiarity.hint: This picks your desktop — the part you actually look at all day.
question.customize.title: Do you like decorating your desktop?
question.customize.hint: Some desktops hand you a paintbrush. Others hand you a finished room.
option.customize.yes: I want to make it mine 🎨
option.customize.no: Working out of the box matters more
question.use.title: What will you mostly do on it?
question.use.hint: Pick as many as you like.
question.gpu.title: What graphics card is in it?
question.gpu.hint: NVIDIA needs slightly more care on Linux. That is all this is about.
result.heading: Start here 🎉
result.disclaimer: This is a starting point, not a verdict. Every option here is a good operating system — if the first one doesn't click, the alternatives are genuinely worth trying.
result.relaxed: Nothing matched every single answer, so these are the closest fits. What we had to bend: {what}.
reason.lightweight.pos: Runs happily in very little memory
reason.lightweight.neg: Wants more memory than this machine has
reason.fits-memory.pos: Comfortable in the memory you have
reason.fits-memory.neg: Tight on the memory you have
reason.no-terminal.pos: Everything can be done through graphical tools
reason.no-terminal.neg: You would end up in the terminal sooner or later
reason.beginner-friendly.neg: Assumes you already know your way around
reason.some-terminal.neg: Expects more command line than you asked for
reason.tinker.pos: Plenty to take apart and rebuild
reason.tinker.neg: Not much here to tinker with
reason.not-beginner-focused.neg: Aimed at newcomers rather than tinkerers
reason.stable-release.neg: Changes underneath you more often than you would like
reason.balanced-release.pos: Fresh software on a schedule you can plan around
reason.balanced-release.neg: Moves at a different pace than you asked for
reason.fresh-release.pos: New versions arrive as soon as they are ready
reason.fresh-release.neg: You would wait months for new software
reason.familiar-chromeos.pos: Simple and focused, much like ChromeOS
reason.customizable.pos: Almost every part of it can be changed
reason.out-of-box.pos: Set up and ready the moment it is installed
reason.out-of-box.neg: Expects you to finish setting it up
reason.good-office.pos: Great for web browsing and documents
reason.good-office.neg: Not really aimed at everyday desktop work
reason.good-dev.neg: Not a natural fit for development work
reason.nvidia.pos: NVIDIA drivers are handled for you
reason.nvidia.neg: You would install the NVIDIA driver yourself
reason.firmware.neg: May need extra repositories for drivers and codecs
distro.mint.name: Linux Mint
distro.mint.tagline: The safest first step away from Windows.
distro.ubuntu.name: Ubuntu
distro.ubuntu.tagline: The one everyone has heard of, and the one every guide assumes you run.
distro.kubuntu.name: Kubuntu
distro.kubuntu.tagline: Ubuntu underneath, with a desktop you can bend into any shape.
distro.zorin.name: Zorin OS
distro.zorin.tagline: Built to look and feel like the desktop you already know.
distro.popos.name: Pop!_OS
distro.popos.tagline: Tuned for people who build things, with NVIDIA sorted out of the box.
distro.debian.name: Debian
distro.debian.tagline: The quiet, rock-solid foundation half of the Linux world is built on.
distro.fedora.name: Fedora
distro.fedora.tagline: New Linux technology first, without living on the bleeding edge.
distro.opensuse-leap.name: openSUSE Leap
distro.opensuse-leap.tagline: Enterprise-grade stability with the best graphical setup tools around.
distro.opensuse-tumbleweed.name: openSUSE Tumbleweed
distro.opensuse-tumbleweed.tagline: A rolling release that is genuinely tested, and can roll back.
distro.mx.name: MX Linux
distro.mx.tagline: Light on its feet, and happy on hardware everyone else gave up on.
distro.manjaro.name: Manjaro
distro.manjaro.tagline: Arch's software, with the sharp edges filed off.
distro.endeavouros.name: EndeavourOS
distro.endeavouros.tagline: Arch the way you would build it yourself, minus the week of setup.
distro.cachyos.name: CachyOS
distro.cachyos.tagline: Arch, compiled and tuned for raw speed, with gaming in mind.
distro.bazzite.name: Bazzite
distro.bazzite.tagline: Console-style gaming that updates itself and is very hard to break.
distro.nobara.name: Nobara
distro.nobara.tagline: Fedora with all the gaming and media fixes already applied.
distro.ubuntu-studio.name: Ubuntu Studio
distro.ubuntu-studio.tagline: A full creative studio — audio, video, graphics — installed and ready.
distro.omarchy.name: Omarchy
distro.omarchy.tagline: An opinionated, keyboard-driven Arch setup for developers who live in a terminal.
distro.ubuntu-server.name: Ubuntu Server
distro.ubuntu-server.tagline: The home-server default, with more tutorials written for it than anything else.
distro.fedora-asahi.name: Fedora Asahi Remix
distro.fedora-asahi.tagline: The only real Linux for Apple Silicon Macs, and it is remarkably good.
